subject: Integration QA: Datadog Agent Auto-Mapper and OTel Trace Sampling
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lee <sara.lee@datadog.com>, Alex Rivera <alex@observantlabs.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Integration QA: Datadog Agent Auto-Mapper and OTel Trace Sampling

Hi Sara and Alex,

Thanks again for the sync earlier — this thread is to lock down a short, operational QA plan for the Datadog agent auto-mapper and how OpenTelemetry sampling rules will interact with our inference runtime. Goal: validate that metrics, traces, and logs align under realistic load while keeping our observability costs predictable.

Proposed high-level steps (please confirm feasibility):
1) Deploy the Datadog agent with the auto-mapper profile from attachment (datadog-agent-autotag-config.yaml) to a Redwood staging cluster.
2) Configure OTel collector sampling matrix (see otel-sampling-matrix.xlsx) with three tiers: full (100%), canary (10%), baseline (1%).
3) Run a 2-hour synthetic load (token-level distribution attached) that exercises streaming, long-context, and reranking paths.
4) Validate: a) span-to-log correlation (trace IDs present in logs), b) correct metric tags from the auto-mapper (model.name, hardware.type, route.name), c) rate-limited ingestion and cost delta measured in Datadog.
5) Acceptance checklist: no missing spans >0.5% of requests, tag completeness >= 98%, and estimated ingest cost delta <= 8% of baseline.

Attachments: datadog-agent-autotag-config.yaml, otel-sampling-matrix.xlsx, and a draft mutual action plan (redwood-mutual-action-plan.md).

Questions for you:
- Sara: can Datadog run a side-by-side ingest estimate for the three sampling tiers so we can sign off on the cost target?
- Alex: any constraints from the Observant Labs OTel collector side we should account for (batching/queue sizes, resource headroom)?

Timeline suggestion: perform canary on Monday 10/19 during the 10:00–12:00 PDT window, then full staging run on 10/20 if canary looks good.

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Partner Engineering
Redwood Inference

---

Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration QA: Datadog Agent Auto-Mapper and OTel Trace Sampling

Thanks Rishi — this plan looks sensible. A few notes from the Datadog side: we can provide an ingest impact estimate using the supplied sampling matrix; we'll run the estimate off your token distribution and a conservative tag-cardinality model. Expect that by EOD Friday we'll have an estimated monthly ingest delta for the three tiers.

Two practical items to confirm before canary:
- Tag naming: please confirm you want model.name and model.version as separate tags (preferred) rather than a single model:version compound. High-cardinality risk if you push model.version per micro-release.
- Agent resource footprint: the auto-mapper adds ~40–60MB RSS on a typical agent; is that acceptable on your staging nodes?

Proposed canary config (we can change):
- Sampling: 10% for traces, but keep metrics 100% (metrics are cheap compared to traces for your workload).
- Span retention: keep full spans for 24 hours in staging, then downsample to summaries if passing acceptance.

I attached a short runbook note (we'll upload a full runbook to the Drive link once we validate). We'll also add a temporary Grafana dashboard (Natalie, can you create the RBAC view we discussed?)

Onboarding items from your side that would speed things up: a test API key with ingest limits and a shared Drive folder for post-run artifacts (screenshots, queries, cost calc).

--
Sara Lee
Integration Engineer, Datadog
Sara.Lee@datadog.com

Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration QA: Datadog Agent Auto-Mapper and OTel Trace Sampling

Appreciate the quick response, Sara. Quick answers inline and an updated mutual action plan summary below.

- model tags: we'll use model.name and model.version as separate tags, but we'll gate detailed model.version tagging behind a sampling rule so we only tag 1% of requests with full version metadata to avoid cardinality explosions.
- agent footprint: confirmed acceptable on staging (Camila has ok'd node sizing).

Mutual action plan (short):
A) Pre-canary (by 10/18 EOD)
  - Redwood: provide test API key, deploy agent config to staging namespace, upload synthetic token distribution. (Owner: Rishi)
  - Datadog: run ingest estimate, share runbook stub, prepare temporary dashboard. (Owner: Sara)
  - Observant Labs: validate OTel collector sampling config and queue sizing. (Owner: Alex)

B) Canary window (10/19 10:00–12:00 PDT)
  - Deploy canary config (10% traces, metrics 100%) to a single AZ, monitor: error rates, span/log correlation, metric tags. Escalation if missing spans >0.5% or unexpected 5xx spike.

C) Staging validation (10/20)
  - Full 2-hour run, collect dashboards and cost estimate, compare against acceptance checklist. Decision: move to staging-wide rollout or revert.

D) Post-run artifacts (within 24 hours of run)
  - Shared Drive folder with: dashboard screenshots, query snippets, ingest delta calc, acceptance checklist signed off by Redwood and Datadog.

Camila: can you confirm the deployment window and whether Platform Ops will be available to rollback if needed?

Sara/Natalie/Alex: please confirm owners and I'll convert this into a formal M.A.P. in the Drive.

Thanks,
Rishi
